title: Beach cover shawl
subtitle: A large open-mesh rectangle in cotton sport weight for beach and poolside.
excerpt: A wide mesh rectangle in sport weight cotton doubles as a shawl, beach blanket, and pool cover-up. The open mesh dries fast and the generous 200 x 90 cm size wraps comfortably. One simple stitch repeat all the way through.
sourceNotes: Open mesh crochet in cotton for beach and summer use has been a popular pattern category since the mid-20th century in both American and British pattern magazines. This version is original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A repeating grid of chains and single stitches that creates an open fabric with large, regular holes.
The initial row of chains from which the rest of the piece is worked, setting the width of a flat crochet piece.
A final row of double crochet worked around the perimeter of a piece to give the edges a firm, even finish.

crochet.gaugeText: 12 mesh sts x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in cotton sport weight with a 4 mm hook.

content.text: A beach cover shawl is a 200 x 90 cm rectangle of
worked in cotton sport weight on a 4 mm hook. Cotton dries fast and the large holes in the mesh mean even less fabric to hold water. The piece is light enough to fold into a beach bag.
The whole pattern is one stitch repeat: one treble, two chains, skip two stitches. That is the entire fabric, worked back and forth across 200 rows until the rectangle is 90 cm wide. A
round at the end gives the perimeter a firm edge.

items.name: Sport weight cotton yarn
items.substitutions: Any smooth sport or DK cotton works. Mercerised cotton dries fastest.

content.text: 12 mesh sts x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in cotton sport weight with a 4 mm hook. At 12 mesh stitches per 10 cm, the 200 cm length needs 240 stitches across the
. Each mesh square is (1 tr, ch 2, skip 2), so 80 mesh squares x 3 sts each = 240 sts, plus a 5-ch setup = ch 245 to start.
Ch 245. Row 1 (wrong side): 1 tr into 6th ch from hook (first mesh square). *Ch 2, skip 2 ch, 1 tr into next ch.* Repeat to end. Turn. (80 mesh squares, 200 cm.)
Ch 5 (counts as 1 tr, ch 2). 1 tr into first tr of previous row. *Ch 2, 1 tr into next tr.* Repeat across, ending 1 tr into the 3rd ch of the turning ch. Turn.
The row 2 pattern is the entire fabric. Work the same row until the piece measures 90 cm from the foundation row. At 8 rows per 10 cm, this is 72 rows.

around all four sides: 1 dc into each tr and 2 dc into each ch-2 space along the long edges, and 1 dc into each row end along the short edges. Work 2 dc into each corner. Join with sl st and fasten off.
Rinse in fresh water after beach or pool use. Wring gently and hang to dry or lay flat. The open mesh dries in under an hour in sun and wind. Machine wash on a gentle cold cycle.

attrs.heading: Common problems
attrs.intro: Mesh beach shawls have simple, practical fixes.

items.symptom: Stitch count drifting after several rows
items.cause: Skipping the turning chain as a stitch
items.fix: The ch-5 at the start of each row is 1 tr plus a ch-2 space. Count it as the first mesh square. The final tr of the row goes into the 3rd chain of the previous row's ch-5, not into the first tr.
Work the foundation chain on a hook one size larger, then swap to the 4 mm for the mesh rows. A tight foundation causes the bottom edge to pull in.

items.symptom: Yarn running out before the width is reached
items.fix: Cotton is heavier than wool at the same weight label. Weigh the yarn rather than relying on the label length. Each 100 g ball of sport cotton covers approximately 18 rows at 200 cm width.
